subject: math
title: Halves, Thirds and Fourths
seo_title: Grade 2 Halves, Thirds and Fourths Worksheets: Equal Shares of Circles and Rectangles
standard_text: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them. Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 halves, thirds and fourths worksheets with pictures: rows and columns of squares, equal or not equal shares, naming halves, thirds and fourths, the whole as 2 halves or 4 fourths, and equal shares with different shapes. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Equal shares are the same size. 2 shares are halves, 3 are thirds, 4 are fourths.
key_sub: The whole is 2 halves, 3 thirds or 4 fourths. More shares means smaller shares, so a half is bigger than a fourth. Equal shares can have different shapes: a triangle and a strip can both be a fourth of the same square.
body_html:
Equal shares

To share fairly, cut a shape into equal shares. Equal shares are all the same size.

Halves, thirds and fourths

2 equal shares are halves. 3 equal shares are thirds. 4 equal shares are fourths (also called quarters).

Equal sharesNameOne shareThe whole
2halvesa half (half of)2 halves
3thirdsa third (a third of)3 thirds
4fourths (quarters)a fourth (a quarter of)4 fourths

In Grade 3 you will write a half as 12. For now, use the words.

The whole

All the shares together make the whole.

Same size, different shape

Equal shares do not have to be the same shape. They only need to be the same size.

Rows and columns of squares

A rectangle can be cut into rows and columns of same-size squares. Rows go across. Columns go up and down.

Example

Mia shares a pizza fairly with 2 friends. What share does each person get?

Mia and 2 friends are 3 people. 3 equal shares are thirds.

Answer: a third of the pizza

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting pieces without checking they are equalFirst check that all the shares are the same size
Thinking a third is bigger than a half because 3 is more than 2More shares means smaller shares. A half is bigger
Counting the cut lines instead of the sharesCount the shares: 2 lines can make 3 or 4 shares
Thinking shares of different shapes cannot be equalCheck the size, not the shape
Adding rows and columns: 3 rows, 4 columns → 7Count by rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12

faq.q: What are equal shares in 2nd grade math?
faq.a: Equal shares are pieces of a shape that are all the same size. A circle cut into 4 same-size pieces has 4 equal shares, called fourths.

faq.q: Is a third bigger than a half?
faq.a: No. When the same shape is cut into more shares, each share is smaller. A half of a pizza is bigger than a third, and a third is bigger than a fourth.

faq.q: Is a fourth the same as a quarter?
faq.a: Yes. A fourth and a quarter both mean 1 of 4 equal shares. 4 fourths, or 4 quarters, make 1 whole.

faq.q: Do equal shares have to be the same shape?
faq.a: No. Equal shares must be the same size, not the same shape. A square cut corner to corner into 4 triangles and a square cut into 4 strips both show fourths.

items.q: How many squares are there in all?
items.e: There are 2 rows with 3 squares in each row. Count by rows: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.

items.q: How many same-size squares make this rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 3 squares in each row. Count by rows: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 squares.

items.q: How many squares are there in all?
items.e: There are 2 rows with 5 squares in each row. Count by rows: 5 + 5 = 10 squares.

items.q: How many same-size squares make this rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 4 squares in each row. Count by rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 squares.

items.q: How many squares are there in all?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 2 squares in each row. Count by rows: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 squares.

items.q: How many same-size squares make this rectangle?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 5 squares in each row. Count by rows: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 squares.

items.q: How many rows and columns does this rectangle have?
items.e: Rows go across. Columns go up and down. Count the squares, not the lines: 2 rows and 4 columns. That is 4 + 4 = 8 squares.

items.q: How many rows and columns does this rectangle have?
items.e: Rows go across. Columns go up and down. Count the squares, not the lines: 3 rows and 5 columns. That is 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 squares.

items.q: How many rows and columns does this rectangle have?
items.e: Rows go across. Columns go up and down. Count the squares, not the lines: 4 rows and 3 columns. That is 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 squares.

items.q: Ava is cutting this rectangle into same-size squares. When the cutting is done, how many squares will there be?
items.e: Only 6 squares are drawn so far. The rectangle will have 3 rows of 4 squares: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 squares.

items.q: Eli is cutting this rectangle into same-size squares. When the cutting is done, how many squares will there be?
items.e: Only 7 squares are drawn so far. The rectangle will have 4 rows of 4 squares: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 squares.

items.q: Zoe is cutting this rectangle into same-size squares. When the cutting is done, how many squares will there be?
items.e: Only 7 squares are drawn so far. The rectangle will have 2 rows of 6 squares: 6 + 6 = 12 squares.

items.q: A rectangle is cut with 1 line across and 2 lines down. All the pieces are same-size squares. How many squares are there?
items.e: 1 line across makes 2 rows. 2 lines down make 3 columns. 2 rows of 3: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.

items.q: A rectangle is cut with 2 lines across and 3 lines down. All the pieces are same-size squares. How many squares are there?
items.e: 2 lines across make 3 rows. 3 lines down make 4 columns. 3 rows of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 squares.

items.q: A rectangle is cut with 1 line across and 4 lines down. All the pieces are same-size squares. How many squares are there?
items.e: 1 line across makes 2 rows. 4 lines down make 5 columns. 2 rows of 5: 5 + 5 = 10 squares.

items.q: A rectangle is cut with 3 lines across and 3 lines down. All the pieces are same-size squares. How many squares are there?
items.e: 3 lines across make 4 rows. 3 lines down make 4 columns. 4 rows of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 squares.

items.q: A muffin pan has 3 rows. Each row has 4 cups. How many cups are in the pan?
items.e: 3 rows of 4. Add a row at a time: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 cups.

items.q: A window has 2 rows of square panes. There are 5 panes in each row. How many panes are there?
items.e: 2 rows of 5. Add a row at a time: 5 + 5 = 10 panes.

items.q: A chocolate bar has 4 rows and 5 columns of squares. How many squares are there?
items.e: 4 rows of 5. Add a row at a time: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 squares.

items.q: Grace makes a quilt with 4 rows of 4 squares. How many squares are in the quilt?
items.e: 4 rows of 4. Add a row at a time: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 squares.

items.q: Is this square cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 2 pieces and both are the same size. So the square shows 2 equal shares: halves. Count the pieces, not the lines: 1 line makes 2 pieces.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 3 pieces, but they are not the same size. Some pieces are bigger than others, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 3 pieces and they are all the same size. So the circle shows 3 equal shares: thirds.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 4 pieces and they are all the same size. So the circle shows 4 equal shares: fourths. Count the pieces, not the lines: 2 lines make 4 pieces.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 2 pieces, but they are not the same size. One piece is much bigger than the other, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 4 pieces, but they are not the same size. Some pieces are bigger than others, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 2 pieces and both are the same size. So the circle shows 2 equal shares: halves. Count the pieces, not the lines: 1 line makes 2 pieces.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 3 pieces, but they are not the same size. Some pieces are bigger than others, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 2 pieces, but they are not the same size. One piece is much bigger than the other, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 4 pieces and they are all the same size. So the rectangle shows 4 equal shares: fourths. Count the pieces, not the lines: 2 lines make 4 pieces.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 4 pieces, but they are not the same size. Some pieces are bigger than others, so these are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? If yes, how many?
items.e: There are 3 pieces and they are all the same size. So the rectangle shows 3 equal shares: thirds. Count the pieces, not the lines: 2 lines make 3 pieces.

items.q: Each shape has 2 pieces. Which shape is cut into equal shares?
items.e: All four shapes have 2 pieces, so counting is not enough. Only in shape D are all the pieces the same size. It shows halves.

items.q: Each shape has 3 pieces. Which shape is cut into equal shares?
items.e: All four shapes have 3 pieces, so counting is not enough. Only in shape C are all the pieces the same size. It shows thirds.

items.q: Each shape has 4 pieces. Which shape is cut into equal shares?
items.e: All four shapes have 4 pieces, so counting is not enough. Only in shape A are all the pieces the same size. It shows fourths.

items.q: Each shape has 2 pieces. Which shape is not cut into equal shares?
items.e: In shape D some pieces are bigger than others. The other three shapes have 2 pieces that are all the same size.

items.q: Each shape has 3 pieces. Which shape is not cut into equal shares?
items.e: In shape D some pieces are bigger than others. The other three shapes have 3 pieces that are all the same size.

items.q: Each shape has 4 pieces. Which shape is not cut into equal shares?
items.e: In shape A some pieces are bigger than others. The other three shapes have 4 pieces that are all the same size.

items.q: Each shape has 4 pieces. Which shape is cut into equal shares?
items.e: All four shapes have 4 pieces, so counting is not enough. Only in shape C are all the pieces the same size. It shows fourths.

items.q: Each shape has 3 pieces. Which shape is cut into equal shares?
items.e: All four shapes have 3 pieces, so counting is not enough. Only in shape A are all the pieces the same size. It shows thirds.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So half of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So half of the rectangle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the square is shaded?
items.e: The square has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So half of the square is shaded.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 3 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a third of the circle is shaded. Count all 3 shares, not only the 2 white ones.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 3 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a third of the rectangle is shaded. Count all 3 shares, not only the 2 white ones.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 3 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a third of the rectangle is shaded. Count all 3 shares, not only the 2 white ones.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a fourth of the circle is shaded. Count all 4 shares, not only the 3 white ones.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a fourth of the rectangle is shaded. Count all 4 shares, not only the 3 white ones.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded. So a fourth of the rectangle is shaded. Count all 4 shares, not only the 3 white ones.

items.q: What are the shares of this circle called?
items.e: There are 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are called fourths. Count the shares, not the 2 lines.

items.q: What are the shares of this rectangle called?
items.e: There are 3 equal shares. 3 equal shares are called thirds. Count the shares, not the 2 lines.

items.q: What are the shares of this rectangle called?
items.e: There are 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are called fourths. Count the shares, not the 3 lines.

items.q: What are the shares of this circle called?
items.e: There are 3 pieces, but the middle piece is bigger than the two side pieces. Thirds must be equal shares, so these are not thirds.

items.q: A shape is cut into 4 equal shares. What is 1 share called?
items.e: 4 equal shares are fourths. So 1 share is a fourth of the shape. (It is not a third: count the 4 shares, not the 3 that are left.)

items.q: Which is another name for a fourth?
items.e: A fourth is also called a quarter. 4 quarters make a whole, just like 4 quarters make a dollar.

items.q: Which word names 3 equal shares?
items.e: 3 equal shares are called thirds, not threes. Each share is a third.

items.q: Which word names 2 equal shares?
items.e: 2 equal shares are called halves. Each share is a half. (We do not say twos or seconds.)

items.q: Which shape has one third shaded?
items.e: Shape C has 3 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a third is shaded. Check the others: the shares must be equal, and you count all the shares.

items.q: Which shape has one fourth shaded?
items.e: Shape C has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a fourth is shaded. Check the others: the shares must be equal, and you count all the shares.

items.q: Which shape has one half shaded?
items.e: Shape D has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a half is shaded. Check the others: the shares must be equal, and you count all the shares.

sets.title: The whole, and which share is bigger

items.q: The circle is cut into equal shares. Which words name the whole circle?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal shares, so they are halves. Together they make the whole: two halves.

items.q: The rectangle is cut into equal shares. Which words name the whole rectangle?
items.e: The rectangle has 3 equal shares, so they are thirds. Together they make the whole: three thirds.

items.q: The circle is cut into equal shares. Which words name the whole circle?
items.e: The circle has 4 equal shares, so they are fourths. Together they make the whole: four fourths.

items.q: The square is cut into equal shares. Which words name the whole square?
items.e: The square has 4 equal shares, so they are fourths. Together they make the whole: four fourths.

items.q: The circle is cut into equal shares. Which words name the whole circle?
items.e: The circle has 3 equal shares, so they are thirds. Together they make the whole: three thirds.

items.q: How many halves make 1 whole?
items.e: A whole cut into 2 equal shares has 2 halves. 2 halves make 1 whole.

items.q: Leo cuts a pie into thirds. How many thirds are in the whole pie?
items.e: Thirds means 3 equal shares. The whole pie is 3 thirds.

items.q: Mia cuts a pizza into fourths. How many fourths make the whole pizza?
items.e: Fourths means 4 equal shares. The whole pizza is 4 fourths. (It is not 3: count the shares, not the cuts.)

items.q: 2 halves make a whole. How many fourths make a whole?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal shares, so 4 fourths make a whole. 2 fourths make only a half.

items.q: Ben eats 3 thirds of a sandwich. How much of the sandwich does he eat?
items.e: 3 thirds make 1 whole. So Ben eats the whole sandwich, not 3 sandwiches.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole circle?
items.e: The whole circle is four fourths. 1 is shaded, so 3 more must be shaded: 1 + 3 = 4.

items.q: How many more thirds must be shaded to shade the whole rectangle?
items.e: The whole rectangle is three thirds. 1 is shaded, so 2 more must be shaded: 1 + 2 = 3.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole rectangle?
items.e: The whole rectangle is four fourths. 2 are shaded, so 2 more must be shaded: 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of a pizza or a third of the same pizza?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal shares. A third is 1 of 3 equal shares. When the same pizza is cut into more shares, each share is smaller. So half is bigger.

items.q: Which is bigger: a third of a cake or a fourth of the same cake?
items.e: Cutting the same cake into 4 shares makes smaller shares than cutting it into 3. So a third is bigger.

items.q: Which is smaller: half of a sandwich or a fourth of the same sandwich?
items.e: 4 is more than 2, so a fourth is smaller. More shares means smaller shares.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into halves. B is cut into fourths. A half is bigger than a fourth, so A is bigger. (4 is more than 2, but more shares means smaller shares.)

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into thirds. B is cut into halves. A half is bigger than a third, so B is bigger.

items.q: The circles are the same size. Which circle has the biggest shares?
items.e: All four circles are the same size. Circle D is cut into halves, the fewest shares. Fewer shares means bigger shares.

items.q: The rectangles are the same size. Which rectangle has the smallest shares?
items.e: All four rectangles are the same size. Rectangle A is cut into fourths, the most shares. More shares means smaller shares.

sets.title: Same size, different shape, and stories

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Compare the shaded shares.
items.e: Both squares are cut into 4 equal shares, so each shaded share is a fourth of the same square. A triangle and a small square can be the same size.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Compare the shaded shares.
items.e: Both squares are cut in half. Half of a square is the same size, whether the cut goes straight down or corner to corner.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Compare the shaded shares.
items.e: Both squares show fourths. A thin strip and a triangle look different, but each is a fourth of the same square.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Compare the shaded shares.
items.e: Both rectangles are cut into 3 equal shares, so each shaded share is a third of the same rectangle. One is tall and thin, one is short and wide, but they are the same size.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Compare the shaded shares.
items.e: A is cut into fourths. B is cut into halves. A half is bigger than a fourth, so B is bigger.

items.q: Is this square cut into fourths?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and they are all the same size. So they are fourths. Fourths do not have to be squares, and you count the shares, not the 2 lines.

items.q: Are these 2 shares halves?
items.e: Count the small squares in each share: every share has 4 squares. The shares have different shapes, but they are the same size. So they are halves.

items.q: Are these 3 shares thirds?
items.e: Count the small squares in each share: every share has 4 squares. The shares have different shapes, but they are the same size. So they are thirds.

items.q: Are these 2 shares halves?
items.e: Count the small squares: one share has 5 squares and the other has 3. They are not the same size, so they are not halves.

items.q: The squares are the same size. Which square is not cut into fourths?
items.e: In square C the 4 pieces are different sizes. The other squares show fourths: triangles, small squares and strips can all be fourths of the same square.

items.q: Mia shares a pizza fairly with 2 friends. What share of the pizza does each person get?
items.e: Mia and 2 friends are 3 people. The pizza is cut into 3 equal shares, so each person gets a third. Do not forget to count Mia.

items.q: Leo and 3 friends share a sandwich fairly. What share does each person get?
items.e: Leo and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal shares are fourths, so each person gets a fourth.

items.q: Kai folds a paper in half. Then he opens it. How many equal shares does he see?
items.e: One fold makes 2 equal shares: 2 halves. The fold is 1 line, but it makes 2 shares.

items.q: Nora folds a square paper in half. She folds it in half again the other way. Then she opens it. What are the shares?
items.e: The 2 folds cross and make 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths, so the paper is four fourths.

items.q: Ava cuts a pie into halves. Ben cuts the same size pie into fourths. Whose pieces are bigger?
items.e: Ben cut his pie into more shares, so his shares are smaller. Halves are bigger than fourths, so Ava’s pieces are bigger.

items.q: Noah gets a third of a cake. Zoe gets a fourth of the same size cake. Who gets more cake?
items.e: A third is 1 of 3 shares. A fourth is 1 of 4 shares. Fewer shares are bigger, so Noah gets more.

items.q: Sam cuts a cake into 4 pieces. One piece is much bigger than the others. Did he cut the cake into fourths?
items.e: Fourths must be 4 equal shares. Sam has 4 pieces, but they are not the same size, so they are not fourths.

items.q: Ruby eats 2 halves of an apple. How much of the apple does she eat?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Ruby eats the whole apple.

items.q: A brownie is cut into fourths. Omar eats 1 fourth. How many fourths are left?
items.e: The whole brownie is 4 fourths. 4 fourths take away 1 fourth leaves 3 fourths.

items.q: Owen cuts a pan of cornbread into 3 rows and 5 columns of same-size squares. How many pieces are there?
items.e: 3 rows of 5 pieces: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 pieces. (3 + 5 = 8 adds the rows and columns. That is not the number of pieces.)
